html:
Ancient Jewish manuscripts found between 1946 and 1956 in caves near Qumran, on the northwest shore of the Dead Sea. They include the oldest known copies of books of the Hebrew Bible.

A Bedouin shepherd found the first scrolls in a cave in the winter of 1946 to 1947. Bedouin and archaeologists then searched eleven caves and found the remains of some 900 manuscripts, most in fragments, written on leather and papyrus in Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek. They date from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE, the time of the Second Temple.

About a quarter are biblical texts. A complete scroll of Isaiah is about a thousand years older than the previous oldest Hebrew copies, and it is almost the same, which showed how carefully the text had been copied. The rest include rules, hymns and visions of a strict Jewish sect waiting for the end of days. Many scholars link it to the Essenes who lived at Qumran, though this is debated. The scrolls were probably hidden around the time Roman troops destroyed Qumran in 68 CE, during the war that ended with the destruction of the Temple.

The area was then under British rule and later Jordan. Today most scrolls are held in Israel, many in the Shrine of the Book in Jerusalem.
sum: Ancient Jewish manuscripts found between 1946 and 1956 in caves near Qumran, on the northwest shore of the Dead Sea. They include the oldest known copies of books of the Hebrew Bible.
